title: bra-1999-fallen-angel
label: Lesley “Viper” Magnus

won.source: the fed's own pay-per-view card for that date, an “I quit” Hell in the Cell match in which Janus submits and the title is handed to Magnus

note: The fed's own 11 Dec 2000 broadcast once calls her “the Hardcore Champ” in the same breath as showing the Fallen Angel belt on her shoulder -- likely the site's own slip, not a second title.

title: bra-1999-featherweight
label: Jennifer Christian

won.source: the fed's own card for that date, in which Christian pins Angel Dust to become, per the broadcast, the new champion

lost.note: The fed's own 8 January 2001 broadcast already refers to Christian as “the former Featherweight champion” after her defense on 4 December 2000; no document in this pass's own read names the match or the wrestler who took the title from her.

note: Defended successfully against Angel Dust on 4 December 2000 before losing the belt off-page sometime in December 2000.

title: bra-1999-celestial
label: Candi Bratton

won.source: the fed's own year-end pay-per-view broadcast, billed beforehand as a Celestial Championship match against champion Akira Hagawa

note: Billed beforehand as the “Celestial Championship” match; the fed's own call of the finish crowns the winner “Women's World Champion” instead, the only time that name is used for the belt in the surviving record. Filed on the existing Celestial title on same-match, same-holders evidence, not as a second title.

title: bra-1999-middleweight
label: Malibu

won.source: the fed's own year-end pay-per-view broadcast, in which the ring announcer bills the bout for the vacant Women's Middleweight Championship and Malibu pins Shea London to win it

note: The title's founding reign; no earlier holder survives in the record.

lost.note: The fed's own 18 March 2002 broadcast has champion Shea London congratulated on a recent Middleweight title win over Malibu at Crime Spree, the fed's own annual February special; no exact date or match text survives.

title: bra-1999-celestial
label: Tiffany Chandler

won.source: the fed's own 21 July 2002 broadcast, an impromptu title match forced by champion Lindsay Locke

lost.note: Lost the same night to Cassie Hopkins, Delilah Strain's chosen challenger in a wager match staked on Chandler's own title win.

note: No surviving document stages how Lindsay Locke, the outgoing champion, first won the title from Candi Bratton (champion 17 December 2001); an open gap.

title: bra-1999-middleweight
label: Shea London

won.source: the fed's own 18 March 2002 broadcast, in which champion Shea London is congratulated on the win; no match text survives

lost.note: Lost to Abby Hoffman in a steel cage match.

note: Won at Crime Spree, the fed's own annual February special; not itself held, so no exact date or match text survives.

title: bra-1999-celestial
label: Cassie Hopkins

won.source: the fed's own 21 July 2002 broadcast, Delilah Strain's own wager match

note: Won the same night Chandler had taken the title from Lindsay Locke, the fourth change of the title in one broadcast.

title: bra-1999-tagteam
label: Tiffany Lane and Alexandria Parker

lost.note: Lost a three-way match to Bad Seed after Rachel Sabbato pinned Tiffany Lane with a frog splash, unseen by Tiffany's bodyguard Brawn.

note: The outgoing champions, Mixie Locke and Maxine Holmes, carry no founding reign of their own on file; the first attested Tag Team title reign in the held record.

title: bra-1999-fallen-angel
label: Veronica Millions

won.source: the fed's own 21 July 2002 broadcast, which bills the title as the Eastern Continental Championship

lost.note: Lost when the referee stopped the match after Millions lost consciousness in a spinning toe hold on an already-injured leg.

note: Filed on the same title id as the held Fallen Angel Championship per the fed's own 2002 FAQ, which names Eastern Continental as that belt's current name; how Stacey Buffington, the outgoing champion, first took the title from r001's own Lesley Magnus is not documented.

title: bra-1999-celestial
label: Akira Hagawa

won.source: the title's own epitaph: a 2001 “Celestial Tournament” closes out the surviving record with a Heaven-and-Hell cage final between Akira Hagawa and Casey Gaines whose result does not survive

lost.note: The fed's own 5 December 2001 update bills the 17 December pay-per-view main event as a Celestial Championship match with Akira Hagawa the champion defending against Candi Bratton.

note: The undated tournament final the title's own epitaph describes as unresolved may be where this reign began; not asserted here without a dated, held document naming it.
